_about: Second levels of two-letter ccTLDs where every name below is a separate registrant's, which registrable_domain() (api/services/public_suffix.py) reads as public suffixes although no section of the Public Suffix List lists them. The compound-ccTLD heuristic read before 2026-10-28 split each of them (a generic second-level label under a 2-letter ccTLD); the PSL's ICANN section alone would have made every owner under one a single site, whose top-1M rank vouched for the others (2026-10-28 review: 1,262 hosts of the 2026-10-24 feed snapshot, 1,100 of them under co.vu). The PSL's PRIVATE rules of that shape (co.ua, com.de, co.nl …) are taken from the vendored list by public_suffix.private_registries(); this file holds the ones in neither section, each with what it was added on. A zone that is one owner's (web.de: 1&1; com.be: Amazon's, SOA root.amazon.com; id.me, net.hr, in.gr) or a government's (gov.hu, sch.gr) does not belong here: the PSL is right to read it as a name. An entry must keep the heuristic's shape and stay out of the PSL (tests/test_public_suffix.py); scripts/build_extension_scorer_data.py ships the overlay to the extensions (registrySuffixes). Evidence: the 2026-10-24 feed snapshot, crt.sh (distinct names under the zone, 2026-10-28), the zone's SOA, SURBL's two-level-tlds list (https://www.surbl.org/static/two-level-tlds, fetched 2026-10-28) and the Tranco top-1M of 2026-10-21.
